items.title: Vulnerabilities and agency of small technologically advanced states: Finland navigating Sino-US strategic technology competition
items.original_context: This article explores how a small technologically advanced state, exemplified by Finland, seeks to maintain agency and manage security risks in Sino-US strategic technology competition, and what future options experts envision for it. The US and China are presently the only ‘geoeconomic great powers’ with competences across four dimensions: investment leverage, supply chains, critical technologies, and technology standards. Given its close security ties to the United States, Finland is expected to align with it when faced with a choice between technological ecosystems. items.title: Why policy is not enough: Renewable energy adoption in India's commercial buildings
items.original_context: Accelerating renewable energy adoption in commercial buildings is critical for achieving climate targets, yet implementation remains uneven in many emerging economies despite supportive policy reforms. This study examines how India's Energy Conservation (Amendment) Act 2022 and associated renewable energy policies influence renewable energy adoption in the commercial building sector. Drawing on Habermas's theory of communicative action, the study develops the concept of regulated communicative action to explain how institutional conditions shape the translation of policy into organisational practice.
